metadata.title: Breard v. Greene, 523 U.S. 371 (1998) (No. 97-8214)
metadata.creator: Supreme Court of the United States
metadata.description:
Case name: Breard v. Greene

Opinion filed: 1998-04-21

Docket No.: 97-8214

Related Docket Nos.:
• 732

Citations:
• 140 L. Ed. 2d 529
• 118 S. Ct. 1352
• 523 U.S. 371
• 1998 U.S. LEXIS 2465

Case holding summaries:
• habeas corpus proceeding where Court examined whether violation had an effect on the trial
• applying Teague to a post-AEDPA habeas petition
• "[N]either the text nor the history of the Vienna Convention clearly provides a... right of action in United States' courts to set aside a criminal conviction and sentence for violation of consular notification provisions."
• the Vienna Convention "[a]rguably confers on an individual the right to consular assistance following arrest"
• appellant procedurally defaulted his claim under the Vienna Convention by not raising and preserving the issue
• holding that “it is extremely doubtful that [a] violation [of the Vienna Convention] should result in the overturning of a final judgment of conviction without some showing that the violation had an effect on the trial”
• noting that the defendant could not "establish how the Consul would have advised him, how that advice of his attorneys differed from the advice the Consul could have provided, and what factors he considered in electing to reject the plea bargain that the State offered him"
• dealing with state procedural bars
• “Any rights that 17 “contribute to the development of friendly relations among nations.” 21 U.S.T at 79 (emphasis added
• “[W]hen a statute which is subsequent in time is inconsistent with a treaty, the statute to the extent of conflict renders the treaty null.”
• holding that, "absent a clear and express statement to the contrary, the procedural rules of the forum State govern the implementation of the treaty in that State"
• holding that if a treaty and a federal statute conflict, "the one last in date will control the other"
• failure to raise Vienna Convention claim in state court resulted in procedural default in subsequent habeas proceeding because procedural rules of the forum State govern
• suggesting that, absent an effect on the trial, violation of the Vienna Convention will not warrant reversal
• rejecting the argument that the Vienna Convention is the "supreme law of the land," and therefore trumps procedural bars, as "plainly incorrect"
• stating the Vienna Convention arguably confers on an individual the right to consular assistance following arrest, but holding that Breard's claim was procedurally barred and that any showing of prejudice was doubtful
• holding that a foreign state is not a "person" entitled to bring suit under § 1983
• stating that "[t]he Vienna Convention . . . arguably confers on an individual the right to consular assistance following arrest."
• applying the rule that “ ‘an Act of Congress . . . is on a full parity with a treaty, and . . . when a statute which is subsequent in time is inconsistent with a treaty, the statute to the extent of conflict renders the treaty null’ ”
• Vienna Convention "arguably confers" an individual right
• habeas corpus proceeding and denial of petitions for writ of certio- rari
• holding that “absent a clear and express statement to the contrary, the procedural rules of the forum State govern the implementation of the treaty in that State”
• "[A]n Act of Congress ... is on a full parity with a treaty, and ... when a statute which is subsequent in time is inconsistent with a treaty, the statute to the extent of conflict renders the treaty null." (internal quotation marks omitted)
• habeas corpus proceeding where Court examined whether violation had an effect on the trial
• "Even were Breard's Vienna Convention claim properly raised and proven, it is extremely doubtful that the violation should result in the overturning of a final judgment of conviction without some showing that the violation had an effect on the trial."
• Court noted that Article 36 "arguably confers on an individual the right to consular assistance following arrest"
• "The Vienna Convention ... has continuously been in effect since 1969."
• repudiating claim that if Vienna Convention had not been violated defendant would have accepted alleged plea agreement
• "The Vienna Convention which arguably confers on an individual the right to consular assistance following arrest...."
